text:
Planning Kyoto's famous December lantern path? It ended after 2021. What Kyoto does instead is better: radish stew at a temple, the year's last flea markets, and temples where you can ring the bell yourself on New Year's Eve 👇

🔔 Bet you can't guess how many monks it takes to ring Chion-in's bell. Answer here 👉 https://japanbystation.com/kyoto-in-december-2026

Every date comes from Kyoto City's official listings for 2026.

🍲 7–8 DECEMBER

Senbon Shakado simmers huge pots of radish with fried tofu and serves bowls for ¥1,000, 10:00–16:00. It's said to keep illness away.

🛍️ THE LAST MARKETS OF THE YEAR

1️⃣ Toji, 21 December, 8:00–15:00. Antiques, pottery, old kimono and New Year decorations.

2️⃣ Kitano Tenmangu, 25 December, from 6:30. Most stalls are up by about 9:00.

🔔 31 DECEMBER

At Chion-in, 17 monks swing a 4 m log at a bell of about 70 tonnes. Watching is by advance application this year, ¥3,000.

Want to ring one yourself? Kodaiji hands out 108 tickets from 22:00. At Shinnyo-do, Eikando and Mibu-dera you just join the queue.

Our take: plan around one market day and New Year's Eve.
